To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gin2- 1 mutant of Arabidopsis thalianna was substantially delayed in compartment-specific metabolome and proteomic changes upon stress.
the hexokinase 2 mutant gin2-2 shows a delayed response of metabolites to high light, but not cold stress, which correlates with a reduced abundance of proteins involved in ATP generation.

the HXK1-deficient Arabidopsis gin2-1 shows a substantial delay in subcellular re-allocation of metabolites upon exposure to high irradiance, and this correlated well with a reduction in proteins of the ATP producing electron transfer chain, while fewer changes in proteins were observed in cold stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatio-temporal dynamics of metabolites and proteins in Arabidopsis plants exposed to abiotic stress.
the subcellular dynamics of primary metabolism and its regulation in plants under abiotic stress, with a focus on high light and cold.
the spatio-temporal dynamics of metabolites and proteins in the context of abiotic stress, and the role of HXK1 in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gin2-2 mutant has a reduced capacity to adapt to high irradiance, but not to cold stress.
the gin2- 1 mutant is impaired in its capacity to respond to stress by a rapid reallocation of metabolites, and that this is a key component of the stress tolerance of the wildtype.
the gin2- 1 mutant shows a different subcellular response to high light stress, and this may contribute to a slower recovery from stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HXK1-defective gin2-1 Arabidopsis mutant is impaired in its ability to re-allocate metabolites and proteins between cellular compartments in response to high light stress, and that this may result from a failure to recruit specific metabolites to their respective subcellular compartments.
the HXK1-dependent sugar sensing mechanism is required for a rapid response to high light and the cold.
HXK1 has an impact on subcellular distribution of metabolites and proteins in response to abiotic stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gin2- 1 mutant of Arabidopsis thalliana is substantially delayed in sub-cellular redistribution of metabolite under high irradiance, and this correlated to a massive reduction in the electron transport chain proteins in the mitochondria, which is not seen under cold.
the HXK1-deficient mutant gin2- 1 is substantially delayed in sub-cellular redistribution of metabolite pools upon high light stress, but not cold stress.

the HXK1 mutant gin2 has a slower and less efficient response to high irradiance, which may be caused by a delayed subcellular redistribution process of metabolites and proteins, and a failure to recruit metabolites specifically protecting individual compartments.
